baslik: Bir sahabe, bir ayet: Ebû Talha ve Beyruhâ

cumleler.metin: Ayet inince, en sevdiği bahçeyi Allah yoluna adadı.
Ebû Talha, Medine'de hurmalığı en çok olan Ensârîydi.
En sevdiği mal, mescidin karşısındaki Beyruhâ bahçesiydi.
Resûlullah oraya girer, güzel suyundan içerdi.
Allah sana nereyi gösterirse oraya koy.”
Ebû Talha da bahçeyi akrabaları ve amcaoğulları arasında paylaştırdı.
İnsan sevdiğini, ancak daha değerli bir sevgiliye ulaşacağına yakîn olunca verir.
Selef de sevdiği şeyi, ihtiyaç duyacakları gün için Allah'a azık yapardı.

planlar.istem: Wide establishing view of a small oasis town at first light: low flat-roofed mud-brick houses half hidden among dense date palms, a thin thread of hearth smoke rising straight up, black volcanic rock scattered in the near foreground, pale gold sky above distant bare hills.

Inside a vast date palm grove: rows of tall rough trunks receding into warm haze, low sun cutting between the fronds, heavy clusters of ripening dates hanging overhead, a narrow irrigation channel glinting along the ground.

A walled garden seen through its open gateway: a stone-lined well at the center with a palm-wood frame, coiled rope and a leather bucket, lush palms and a few pomegranate bushes around it, sunlit mud-brick wall behind.
Close view of clear water just drawn from a well: a leather bucket brimming and dripping over the worn stone rim, sunlight sparkling in the falling drops, wet dark stone, cool palm shade around.

Low angle from the ground beneath a palm tree: an empty woven palm mat in the shade where someone has just risen, faint sandal prints in the dust leading away toward a bright gateway in a mud-brick wall.
A whole palm garden seen from its gate at golden hour: every frond glowing, the stone well small in the distance at the end of a straight earthen path, long shadows lying across the ground.
A heavy palm-wood garden gate swung wide open, its wooden bar lifted out and leaning against the mud-brick wall, warm light pouring through the opening onto the empty path beyond.
View from above the crowns of a palm grove toward a low mud-brick town on the horizon, the fronds forming a dark green sea, one clear path of light running through the middle distance.
Looking up from the ground through palm fronds into strong slanting beams of late sunlight, the beams made visible by fine dust in the air, dark trunks framing both sides.
Looking up from the ground through palm fronds into strong slanting beams of late sunlight, the beams made visible by fine dust in the air, dark trunks framing both sides.
A palm garden seen from a height, divided by low mud-brick walls and palm-frond fences into several smaller plots, each with its own palms, a small water channel branching to feed every plot.

Night interior of a plain mud-brick room: a single clay oil lamp burning on a low wooden stand, a closed leather-bound volume resting beside it, a small square window showing a deep blue sky with stars.
